[[File:2006 WCHA Final Five.jpg|thumb|The Wild have played their home games at the [[Grand Casino Arena]] since its first season.]]
The [[Minnesota Wild]] is an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]]. It plays in the [[Central Division (NHL)|Central Division]] of the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=National Hockey League|accessdate=2008-12-22}}</ref> The Wild joined the NHL in 2000 as an [[expansion team]] with the [[Columbus Blue Jackets]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Pincus|first=Arthur|year=2006|title=The Official Illustrated NHL History|publisher=Reader's Digest|isbn=0-88850-800-X}}</ref> The Wild have played their home games at the [[Grand Casino Arena]] since its first season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xcelenergycenter.com/arena.jsp |title=Arena Info |publisher=Grand Casino Arena |accessdate=2008-12-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216062050/http://www.xcelenergycenter.com/arena.jsp |archivedate=2008-12-16 }}</ref> The majority of the Wild is owned by [[Craig Leipold]], and [[Bill Guerin]] is their [[general manager]].

There have been six&nbsp;[[head coach]]es for the Wild franchise. [[Jacques Lemaire]], who coached the team from its inception to the end of the [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09 season]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=417874|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090413162412/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=417874|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 13, 2009|title=Lemaire calls it quits in Minnesota|publisher=National Hockey League|date=2009-04-11|accessdate= 2009-04-20}}</ref> compiled a record of 574 regular-season games coached, 253 regular-season games won, 605 regular-season [[Point (ice hockey)|points]], a .527 regular-season [[winning percentage]], 29 playoff games coached, 11 playoff games won, and a .379 playoff winning percentage with the Wild. Lemaire was awarded the [[Jack Adams Award]] with the Wild in the [[2002–03 NHL season|2002–03 season]]. [[Todd Richards (ice hockey)|Todd Richards]] was hired two months after Lemaire's resignation and fired in April 2011.<ref name="RichardsHired">{{cite web|url=http://license.icopyright.net/user/viewContent.act?tag=3.5721%3Ficx_id=D98RD4O84|title=Wild hire Todd Richards as head coach|agency=Associated Press|accessdate=2009-06-15|date=2009-06-15|archive-date=2020-05-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200524195417/http://license.icopyright.net/user/viewContent.act?tag=3.5721%3Ficx_id%3DD98RD4O84%2F|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Mike Yeo]] was hired by the club in June 2011 and fired in February 2016. [[John Torchetti]] was named interim head coach.  On May 7, [[Bruce Boudreau]] was signed to a four-year deal as the new head coach, just 8 days after being released by the [[Anaheim Ducks]].

On February 14, 2020, [[Bruce Boudreau]] was released by the [[Minnesota Wild]] following a disappointing first half of the [[2019–20 NHL season|2019–20 season]]. This included Boudreau making a paperwork error that left the Wild with five defensemen in a game on January 15. [[Dean Evason]] was named as interim head coach, previously being assistant coach. On July 13, 2020, Evason was hired as the full-time head coach, with a contract extension through the 2021–22 season. Evason was later fired on November 27, 2023, after a poor start to the [[2023–24 NHL season|2023–24 season]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Head Coach Dean Evason and Assistant Coach Bob Woods Relieved of Duties |url=https://www.nhl.com/wild/news/minnesota-wild-relieve-coaches-of-duties-112723 |website=NHL.com |access-date=November 28, 2023 |date=November 27, 2023}}</ref> and [[John Hynes (ice hockey)|John Hynes]] was named the new head coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Wild Names John Hynes Head Coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/wild/news/minnesota-wild-hires-hynes-112723 |website=NHL.com |access-date=November 28, 2023 |date=November 27, 2023}}</ref>
